title: Finite-field bounded constructibility predicates agree
statement: For a scheme X separated and of finite type over a field k, the bounded constructibility predicate defined by finite constant coefficient models [sk-def-sfb-constructible] equals the upstream bounded-cohomology and stratified-local-finite-presentation predicate [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], both for the specified condensed algebraic closure of Q_l and for every finite coefficient field E inside it [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set].

source.place: Models persist and finite Postnikov induction: identify the finite-constant-model convention with the finite-field constructible convention before applying the cone induction.

proof.text: Finite type over k makes X Noetherian and therefore qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. On X the finite-constant-model constructibility condition uses one finite stratification, just as the upstream predicate. Every locally closed stratum is topologically Noetherian because its immersion is an embedding.

A finite constant local model is locally finitely presented by [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Transport along the invertible Cartesian coefficient pullback [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] to identify the two restriction conventions on each stratum. This proves finite-constant-model constructibility implies upstream constructibility.

Conversely transport a locally finitely presented restriction to the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring on each stratum. The finite-field local-freeness theorem [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality], or its algebraic-closure counterpart [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qbar-lfp-local-triviality], supplies a pro-etale finite-free trivializing cover. The private finite_lf and algcl_lf interfaces of CondensedConstructibleSerre implement the universe and coefficient transport. Transport finite freeness through the coefficient pullback isomorphism on each covering member.

The inverse image of the rank-n regular condensed module is the rank-n regular coefficient module: inverse image and its module functor preserve finite sums and the regular module. The condensed free module is finitely presented by the zero morphism from rank n to rank n and the cokernel-of-zero isomorphism. These objects give genuine finite constant local models, including n=0, with the same covers and stratification. Thus both module predicates agree. Apply this equivalence to every cohomology object; both derived predicates have definitionally the same boundedness condition, so function and proposition extensionality give their equality.
